newsitem.title: CHINA: Newcomer pushes Shenzhen B index to 97 low close.
newsitem.headline: Newcomer pushes Shenzhen B index to 97 low close.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index recorded its lowest close for 1997 on Wednesday, pulled down by weighty Bengang Steel Plates Co Ltd, but analysts said the index was likely to hold steady in the near future.

The Hong Kong dollar-denominated B share index sagged 0.87 points or 0.71 percent to 120.44, after hitting a 1997 all-time low of 118.69 points. Turnover shrank to HK$94.0 million from HK$287.9 million on Tuesday.
The A share index gained 5.17 points or 1.35 percent to 387.44. Turnover was 4.7 billion yuan against Tuesday's 5.3 billion.
"Bengang is the most heavily weighted stock in the B share market, and its poor performance today significantly dragged down the index," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.

The steel company on Tuesday listed 400 million B shares at HK$2.38 each. It closed at HK$2.35 to become the first new stock this year to lose out on its debut, as investors turned away from China's ailing steel sector, analysts said.
On Wednesday, Bengang plunged HK$0.15 or 6.38 percent to HK$2.20. Trading volume reached 23 million shares worth of HK$50.8 million.
Analysts said the B index appeared to have bottomed out, although few expected a bull run ahead.
"There is just not much room for the index to fall, as most of this year's gains have been wiped out," the Guotai analyst said.
An analyst at J&A Securities said: "There is nothing to lift the market mood. It's pretty grim at the moment."
Investors lost confidence when the July 1 Hong Kong handover from British to Chinese rule failed to brighten sentiment as had been expected.
Active trade in Hong Kong's red chips -- stocks with Chinese backing, also diverted attention from B shares, analysts said.
Shenzhen's A shares gained on Wednesday on the back of market leader Shenzhen Development Bank, which rose 0.93 yuan or 2.8 percent to 34.0 yuan.
